questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of Covid, I had to choose a location in Europe, and London is a very international and academic city to live in. The language wasn't a turning point for me, but of course, made it all a lot easier and expanded my English language skills. UCL is a great university so this was also an important factor.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything school-related was amazing, and some amazing people but the living situation is a mess!! UCL is also a great university. Remember a full term is only 2,5 months in London, so you will only be on exchange from around late September to mid/late december. You are totally free all of September and January. All exams are written exams (essays), so no exams at school.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to get information from UCL, and the connection between KU and UCL is not great. The system is confusing because the university is so big. You will receive information when you come, but the communication by email or phone is really not good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When we were properly enrolled we got a lot of emails with introduction information. Remember to read ALL emails, as there is deadlines.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They tried to inform, but if something wasn't in an email, it was hard to find the correct person to ask.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: VERY VERY HARD. If you go to London be prepared to use a lot of time on housing, and get ready to be scammed a lot. We were very careful, but the landlords are not interested in renting their place for a short stay of only 3 months, so they are ready to scam you a few days before you move in. If you know anyone in London before you move there, this will be your safest bet at trying to find a place, because it is best to see the place and get a contract straight away.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live by yourself but is a lot of money to spend on something not so nice. I would try to get student accommodation, but that is not always possible. WATCH THE DEADLINE for student-housing applications. We did not receive housing because we missed the date in an email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit complicated because you had to match the courses with the schedule and that didn't always add up. And the process of registering was not able until we came, and then a lot of courses was taken. We then waited a while to actually get the course accepted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose your courses by yourself. 50% has to be from the faculty, and the rest is toyally free. You have to make your own shedule, and therefore no overlaps between courses. This can be quite hard. When registered, with help by a student affiliate officer, you had to write to each professor from each class (4 classes of 7,5 ECTS each) why you would fit the class. Then they had to accept, of they would tell you if it was full. If full you had to look at other courses and make it fit. It took about one week (intro week) and was quite stressfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The affiliate teacher helped a lot. All the professors are very helpful, it just takes time because everyone is busy.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/4 of the classes I wanted, and the fourth the professor was really nice in trying to find a class similar to the one I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would look into the classes you want already before you arrive in London, and make sure they fit in the schedule. And take contact with an affiliate teacher/advisor beforehand and say to them you want to register early to make sure classes are not filled. They will also tell you how to find the email of the professors, to get their approval. You can register when you are enrolled

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really great! Amazing professors. Not a lot of school (2-3 hours every day, and one day off), and no exam preparation but a lot of essays and small deadlines all the time.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level is lower at UCL than KU, simply because there is no physical exams. The education is very academic and profesional, but it is definetly easier as an affiliate because we don't have exams, only essays. You only need 40% to pass, which is not a lot. The papers are often topics you choose your own.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No SAU, only lectures. So a lot of self study, but it works fine with the essay writing part.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cellular Pathology
Introduction to Coding for Bioscience - Python
Biology of ageing
Applied Nutrition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you just have a small interest in coding, the Python course was amazing. The teacher is so amazing, and the course was great fun. 
Cellular Pathology has a great teacher as well, and lecturers that present their own publised reseach. And the exam is 'just' one essay.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food I don't know. You can use a lot less if you eat from home, but in London you eat out a lot at social occasions. 
Housing is very expensive for not a lot. TIP: go a bit north/east from UCL and there is cheaper options, but the ALWAYS look at the metro line. You want to live around max 30 min from UCL with total commute (very normal).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are cheap. And eating out is not the expensive either.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 100+ societies and clubs! You get to meet many people!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nordic Society, Introduction week, sightseeing with friends

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a lot of intro week things, and join the intro events at the societies and clubs during the introduction week.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We went to Edinburgh and Oxford. You can go to many places by train and bus from London.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Usually, you end up meeting the international student, but there are 50% international students at UCL which is great!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture and the many societies and clubs!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Meet up with a lot of people!! Get out there! It scary in the beginning, but so worth it :-) 
Don't think about the grade too much, it will all work out. 
Just call, email or ask questions if you are confused. Many want to help!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friendships and going to another university

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to get new friends!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
